title: India’s dengue burden grows more complex as multiple virus strains circulate together, study finds

analysis.time: Published - July 28, 2026 07:28 pm IST.
analysis.location_and_population: India, across 25 States and Union Territories.
analysis.event: A two-year nationwide surveillance study by the ICMR-VRDL network found that all four dengue virus serotypes are circulating together in several parts of the country, with nearly one in 14 patients infected with more than one serotype at the same time.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study analysed 6,889 laboratory-confirmed dengue samples. DENV-2 remained the predominant serotype, accounting for over half of all infections. Around 7% of patients were infected with two or more dengue serotypes concurrently. Patients with concurrent infections were more likely to develop severe manifestations of dengue, including dangerously low platelet counts, bleeding complications and severe joint pain.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The findings need confirmation through long-term clinical studies. India currently has no dengue vaccine in its Universal Immunisation Programme, although indigenous vaccine candidates are in advanced stages of clinical development, and an internationally approved vaccine recently received regulatory clearance for import and sale in India. Continuous surveillance of circulating serotypes would be critical because vaccine effectiveness varies against different dengue strains.

This hyperendemic transmission poses challenges for future dengue vaccination programs, as vaccine effectiveness varies across different strains. Researchers emphasize the need for continuous surveillance and incorporating dengue vaccines into public health programs, particularly in endemic areas.
